description: The Standard Green Infrastructure Specifications are the construction contract requirements that New York City uses when it builds green infrastructure assets such as right-of-way bioswales and stormwater tree pits. The Department of Design and Construction prepared the 148-page edition of 1 September 2021 for the Department of Environmental Protection. Coverage is New York City projects. Sections set material and workmanship requirements for engineered soil, topsoil, clean open graded stone, geotextile, HDPE pipe and stormwater chambers, steel tree guards, inlet screen boxes, concrete elements, planting of trees and plants, sodding, seeding, plant establishment care, photo documentation and final record documents. Format and access: a PDF download, with later specification bulletins on the department's publications page. Licence: no open licence is stated in the document; free to read. Caveats: these are contract specifications for one city, not test data, and they are updated by bulletin, so the edition date matters. It supports capacity planning and cost estimation for green stormwater infrastructure retrofits. A related catalogue record is the NYC Green Infrastructure Program case study.
